selection_rule: Fixed mechanism-level triage only; no performance metric, holdout outcome, parameter search, asset search or family ranking.

candidates.source: FINRA Reg SHO Daily Short Sale Volume
candidates.mechanism: Abnormal short-sale participation as a crowding/information-flow signal distinct from ordinary OHLCV trend features.
candidates.pit_rule: Use only a completed daily file after verified public availability; act no earlier than the next eligible trading session.
candidates.data_contract: Daily security-level short volume, executed/reported trade date, total volume and stable security identifier mapping.
main_risks: Off-exchange/FINRA-reporting scope differs from consolidated market volume.
Historical public-availability timestamp must be certified.
Short-sale marking is not identical to directional short positioning.

candidates.source: SEC EDGAR Forms 3/4/5 and filing headers
candidates.mechanism: Aggregated open-market insider purchase/sale information as an information-flow signal.
candidates.pit_rule: Use EDGAR acceptance datetime as first public availability; execute no earlier than the next eligible trading session to remove intraday ambiguity.
candidates.data_contract: Raw filing/header retrieval, accession ID, issuer CIK, form type, transaction coding, acceptance datetime and immutable filing cache.
main_risks: Entity/transaction classification must exclude non-economic option and administrative transactions by fixed rule.
SEC bulk insider datasets are quarterly and omit some filing metadata; raw filings remain authoritative.
Historical retrieval completeness must be independently verified.

candidates.mechanism: Macro-information state change measured from the vintage that actually existed at a past date.
candidates.pit_rule: Use the dated vintage available by the decision date and act on the next eligible trading session; no intraday release timestamp is required.
candidates.data_contract: Series IDs, vintage dates, observation dates, first-availability calendar and immutable vintage snapshots.
main_risks: Earlier project attempts had vintage retrieval timeouts.
Release-vintage semantics must remain separate from later revisions.
Composite construction must be fixed before any performance evaluation.

candidates.source: CFTC Commitments of Traders public historical reports
candidates.mechanism: Positioning/crowding state and crowding change as cross-asset information.
candidates.pit_rule: Use only after the actual public release date; scheduled Friday release time is insufficient when historical publication was disrupted.
candidates.data_contract: Report date, actual public-release date, contract identity, trader category, position fields and immutable raw-report cache.
main_risks: 2025 publication interruption created report-date versus actual-publication-date divergence.
Contract-to-equity mapping is a separate fixed design problem.

candidates.source: Wikimedia Analytics Pageviews API/public pageview data
candidates.mechanism: Unexpected change in public attention to a fixed company/article mapping.
candidates.pit_rule: Use only a fully completed daily observation and act on the next eligible trading session.
candidates.data_contract: Frozen issuer-to-page mapping, daily pageviews, agent/access filters, missing-data flags and immutable snapshots.
main_risks: Entity-to-article mapping can create hidden asset selection.
Bots/spiders and page-definition changes require fixed filtering.
Public API data can lag completion of the previous day.

candidates.source: GDELT 2.1 historical event and news files
candidates.mechanism: Firm/sector-level media attention and tone shock as an information-flow layer orthogonal to price-only signals.
candidates.pit_rule: Use only archived records available before the decision cutoff; next-session action; no later article corrections or reprocessing leakage.
candidates.data_contract: Frozen entity mapping, archive file checksum, event/article timestamps, source identifiers and deterministic aggregation.
main_risks: Entity resolution and ticker-to-company ambiguity are substantial.
Source universe and language coverage can drift.
Historical reprocessing/version changes must be fingerprinted.
